questions.title: Why does LongRoPE need to search separate rescale factors for each RoPE dimension?
questions.question_body: In the paper, the authors introduce a variable λ_i for every roasting‑pair dimension instead of using a single global interpolation factor. I can understand that different frequencies might behave differently, but if the original RoPE already captures a range of frequencies, how does having an individual λ per dimension improve performance? What would happen if we kept a single λ for all dimensions?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind the non‑uniform token position threshold (ρ) and how is it used?
questions.question_body: LongRoPE defines ρ as the number of initial tokens immune to interpolation. The method says that early tokens should be interpolated less, but I’m unclear why exactly that matters. Could someone explain in concrete terms how preserving the first ρ positions influences attention patterns or token representations?

questions.title: How does the monotonicity constraint on λ_i (λ_i ≤ λ_{i+1}) guarantee better search efficiency?
questions.question_body: The evolutionary search algorithm checks λ_i ≤ λ_{i+1} before evaluating a candidate. Why should a monotonic sequence of rescale factors be more likely to yield good perplexities? Is there any theoretical basis for this beyond the NTK argument presented in the paper?

questions.title: Why is an 8× extension possible without fine–tuning but a 512× extension still requires fine–tuning?
questions.question_body: The authors mention that by exploiting non‑uniform interpolation they can push LLaMA2’s context from 4k to 32k (8×) with only search, yet reaching 2048k (512×) needs two rounds of fine‑tuning (first to 256k, then a second interpolation). Is this bottleneck purely due to GPU memory limits, or are there theoretical limits on how far interpolation can go without training data covering those lengths?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE recover performance on short contexts after extreme extension?
questions.question_body: After pushing the window to 2048k, the model shows degradation on 4k and 8k sequences. The paper says they rerun an evolutionary search with a smaller max λ. Could you detail how this fine‑tuning step is performed during inference and why it mitigates the crowded‑position problem?

questions.title: Can we interpret the learned λ_i as a reflection of each dimension’s effective frequency range?
questions.question_body: The evolutionary search returns a vector of rescale factors λ_i for each RoPE dimension. Does this vector encode anything meaningful about which dimensions need more stretching or compression? How would one visualize or analyze these λ_i values relative to the original θ frequencies?

questions.title: Is LongRoPE compatible with decoder‑only models using absolute position embeddings?
questions.question_body: The method is presented for models using rotary positional embeddings (RoPE). Could it be adapted to transformer variants that use absolute learnable or sinusoidal embeddings? If so, what changes would be necessary in both the search formulation and the interpolation strategy?

questions.title: Why do existing methods like PI, NTK, and YaRN fail to preserve long‑context perplexity after 2× extension?
questions.question_body: The experiments show perplexity spikes after doubling the context when using linear PI or NTK/YaRN. What specific aspect of these interpolation strategies causes such jumps? Is it due merely to over‑crowding of positions or are there deeper interactions with attention dynamics at play?

questions.title: How does evolutionary search scale when moving from 4k to hundreds of thousands of tokens?
questions.question_body: Equation (4) shows an astronomically large search space for large s values (e.g., s=512). The paper claims evolutionary search still works efficiently. Could anyone explain how population size, mutation probabilities, and constraint enforcement together curtail this complexity? Are there empirical results showing runtime versus target length?

questions.title: Could we use reinforcement learning instead of evolutionary algorithms for optimizing λ_i and ρ?
questions.question_body: Evolutionary algorithms provide stochastic exploration but may require many perplexity evaluations. Would framing this as a RL problem where actions are adjusting λ_i lead to faster convergence? How might such an approach compare in terms of sample efficiency?

questions.title: What is meant by ‘keeping most pre‑existing optimizations’ in LongRoPE?

"The abstract says models extended via LongRoPE retain the original architecture with minor modifications to positional embedding, and can reuse most pre-existing optimizations." Which specific optimizations are preserved (e.g., quantization, FlashAttention) and why do they not interfere with changing RoPE parameters?
